name: PT Menthobi Karyatama Raya Tbk

frontmatter.title: Menthobi Karyatama Raya — a processor priced for an estate it does not own
frontmatter.summary: MKTR buys roughly three quarters of the fruit it mills, so its cost line moves with the CPO price it sells at. Corrected for that pass-through, and for a volume plan the company has already missed once, the last audited spread does not support the price. We cut to SELL.
thesis: A processor, not a planter: 255 kt kt of the 351 kt kt of fruit milled in FY2025 was bought in, so the estate is the smaller half of the economics and the mill spread, not the CPO level, is what compounds [S4, S2].

The deck's US$ US$1,135/t a tonne and a weaker rupiah lift FY2026E EBITDA to 206.7 on 1,500.2 of revenue, an EBITDA margin of 13.8% against 13.4% in FY2025 - flat, because purchased fruit is 857 IDR bn of the Rp921 IDR bn CPO segment cost of revenue and takes the CPO move back [S2].
The volume plan is not new: 82.9 kt kt was also the 2025 target and the company produced 76.7 kt kt, an achievement of 92.5%, so we model the delivery rate, not the target [S4, F3, F31].
The balance sheet carries 340 IDR bn of restricted cash pledged against 757.7 of bank debt, so the reported net debt of 596.6 overstates free liquidity [S2].
At a through-cycle CPO of US$ US$1,150/t a tonne our DCF gives Rp124, the peer multiples Rp72 and Rp76; the price needs CPO near US$ US$1,322/t to hold, so we move to SELL with a Rp79 target [S0].
The dividend is the main cash return: a payout of 40.9% on 4.6 of EPS is a 1.6% yield at the price, thin against a cost of equity of 11.9% [S0].

catalysts.event: B40 biodiesel mandate implementation and the monthly CPO reference resets
Peak Q4-2026 harvest and the first read on bought-in FFB supply for the 2026 plan
FY2026 audited results against the company plan for CPO production and sales
FY2026 dividend decision, the main cash return for minorities

blocks.text: Menthobi Karyatama Raya is the listed palm-oil arm of the Maktour group: two mills and several thousand hectares of estate in Lamandau, Central Kalimantan, producing crude palm oil, palm kernel oil and palm kernel [S4, S2]. It listed in November 2022 and has grown by buying fruit and, once, by buying a mill, not by clearing land [S4, S5].

We move to SELL from HOLD with a Rp79 target against a Rp115 price, a return of -29.4% [S0]. The move is not a change of view on palm oil: it is the correction of the first draft's calculation errors, including a cost pass-through computed on the total-company cash cost instead of the CPO segment's, a volume forecast that took a plan the company had already missed, and a pledged deposit left out of the bridge. The market pays 25.3x of FY2025 earnings and 2.1x of book for a business that earned an ROE of 8.5% in the last audited year [S0, S2]. At the deck's CPO path the DCF is worth Rp124, the peer EV/EBITDA cross-check Rp72 and peer book value Rp76; after the liquidity discount of 30.0% the weighted target is Rp79 [S0].

Our variant view is about the business model rather than the palm price. MKTR is mostly a toll mill: it bought 255 kt kt of the 351 kt kt of fruit it processed in FY2025, and the purchased fruit is priced off CPO, so a higher CPO lifts revenue and the cost line together [S4, S2]. The profit comes from the owned estate's fruit, 106 kt kt, which costs a fraction of the market price to grow [S4]. That is a real asset, but a small one, and the market is paying for it as if the whole throughput carried estate margins.

Three things move the value. The first is CPO: the deck's US$ US$1,135/t a tonne this year and US$ US$1,240/t next, against a long-run anchor of US$ US$1,150/t, is the difference between our FY2026E EBITDA of 206.7 and FY2025's 167.5 [S0, S2]. The second is the pass-through: how much of a CPO move the bought-in fruit price takes back. The third is the capital structure: the DCF bridges off the valuation-date balance sheet, where net debt is already below the year-end figure, and 340 IDR bn of the group's cash is a pledged time deposit that cannot be distributed [S2]. A reversal of the deck's 2027 premium takes the DCF toward the bear value in section five, not to the multiple values.

MKTR operates one estate and two palm oil mills at Kujan and Guci in Lamandau, Central Kalimantan, over a location-permit area of about 12,000 ha ha, of which 8,500 ha ha is planted plantation and 6,000 ha ha of the main subsidiary is planted, with trees averaging ten years of age [S4]. The group also runs a compost and biofertiliser unit and a small seedling and fertiliser trade [S4, S6]. It is a rounding error in the national crop: throughput was 351 kt kt of fruit in FY2025 against a national CPO crop that GAPKI put at 51.7 Mtm tonnes [S4].

The product mix is three oils and a kernel. FY2025 revenue of 1,246.1 was dominated by crude palm oil, with palm kernel oil the second line and palm kernel, palm expeller, seed and fertiliser the remainder [S2]. The CPO segment carried 921 IDR bn of cost of revenue, and the other products earned a 21.9% gross margin on 209.4 of forecast revenue [S2, S4]. Output in FY2025 was 76.7 kt kt of CPO and 6.1 kt kt of PKO from 351 kt kt of fruit [S4].

The intake is the defining fact. 255 kt kt of fruit was bought from third parties and 106 kt kt came from the company's own estates [S4]. The bought-in fruit is paid at a market price that tracks CPO, while own fruit carries the estate's production cost, so the profit pool is concentrated in the smaller volume. Two Indonesian refiners, PT Sinar Alam Permai and PT Citra Borneo Utama, took 77.5% of FY2025 revenue, the first more than half of it, which makes the company a price-taker on both sides of its trade [S2].

Growth has been bought, but not with that mill. In August 2023 MKTR and its subsidiary acquired PT Khatulistiwa Sinergi Omnidaya, a mill with capacity of thirty tonnes of fruit a day, for under twenty billion rupiah [S5]. A mill that size cannot explain the intake step-up between 2024 and 2025; the throughput is bought-in fruit, which supplied 255 kt kt of the 351 kt kt processed, with the estate's own fruit at 106 kt kt [S4, F7, F8, F9]. The FY2025 report sets a short-term strategy of asset optimisation and production capacity, a medium-term one of agribusiness expansion and revenue diversification, and flags a kernel crushing plant and the compost unit as new revenue lines [S4, S6]. The company targets 2026 CPO production of 82.9 kt kt, the same figure it targeted for 2025, with a sales projection and a gross profit the first draft never stated [S4 p.63, F31].

Ownership is concentrated. Fuad Hasan Masyhur held 68.6% at 31 December 2025, PT Maktour Bangun Persada, the family's hajj and umrah travel business, 7.8%, and the public 23.6%, so the two named holders control more than three quarters of a company with no second block to balance them [S4 p.116, S5]. The president director is Harry Mohamad Nadir, and the group's commercial logic is a family agribusiness attached to a travel group rather than an institutional plantation company [S4, S5].

Indonesia is the world's largest palm-oil producer, and the price MKTR receives is set by the domestic reference and the world market, not by the company [S4]. GAPKI put FY2025 national CPO output at 51.7 Mtm tonnes and expects 4.0% growth in 2026 from productivity and tree maturation rather than new land [S4, F28]. The company's own industry review projects CPO at around US$1,050/t a tonne in the year ahead, below the US$1,240/t the deck carries for next year [S4, S0].

Demand policy is the swing factor. The nationwide B40 mandate absorbed 15.6 mn kl million kilolitres of biodiesel in 2025, about 14.0 Mt million tonnes of CPO or roughly a third of the national crop, and the policy discussion points to B45-B50 over 2026-27 [S4 p.258]. Each step up in the blend absorbs more CPO at home, reduces export availability and supports the reference price, which is why the domestic price has not followed every move in the world market down [S4]. On the supply side, GAPKI warned on 13 November 2026 that El Nino and delayed fertiliser applications could cut national output by up to 3.0 Mt Mt in 2027 as the drought reaches the harvest, which is why the deck carries a premium next year before gliding back to its long-run anchor [S7, S0]. For a seller of crude oil to two domestic refiners, the levy and export duty are not a direct cost: they fall on the exporter at the port, and MKTR's realised price already reflects the domestic discount that the wedge creates, so a levy change reaches the company through the reference rather than through a line in the cost of revenue [S2].

Competition is a cost-curve story, and MKTR is not on the low end. Its own fruit cost is competitive because the estate is mature, but most of throughput is bought at market and the mill has no scale advantage against the large integrated groups [S4, S2]. The company discloses no cost per tonne against a public curve, so we place it by inference rather than by quartile: the owned estate sits at the low end, the bought-in majority carries a market-linked cost, and the blended cash cost therefore tracks the reference instead of holding a fixed advantage [S2, F23, F24]. The two customers are themselves processors, Sinar Alam Permai and Citra Borneo Utama, so the refining and kernel-crushing margin that an integrated planter keeps sits with the buyer rather than with MKTR [S2, F22]. The moat is location and the plasma relationships around the mills: fruit is perishable and must be crushed within a day, so the mill's catchment is a real barrier to a new entrant, but it does not protect the margin when CPO falls and the bought-in fruit price lags [S2, S4]. Five forces are unfavourable on the customer side, given the two-buyer concentration, neutral on suppliers because fruit is bought at a published reference, and favourable against new entrants because of the mill catchment and land permitting [S2].

The macro frame matters mostly through the rupiah. The house regime is balance-of-payments pressure with a cautious tilt, the commodity bloc is neutral, and the rupiah is forecast at Rp17,570/USD this year against Rp16,448/USD in FY2025 [S0]. Because costs are rupiah and CPO is dollar-priced, a weaker rupiah widens the rupiah spread even when the dollar price is flat, and that is a genuine part of the FY2026E uplift.

The FY2025 accounts show the model clearly. Revenue was 1,246.1, cost of revenue 1,056.7 and gross profit 189.4, a gross margin of 15.2% that fell from FY2024 because the bought-in fruit price rose faster than CPO, as the audited segment economics show [S2, F5, F6]. Operating expenses were 70.6, EBIT 118.8 and net profit 54.9 [S2]. Those FY2025A operating-expense and EBIT lines are the restated history: they include the non-cash share-option charge that the forecast opex ratio excludes, which is why the forecast EBITDA margin of 13.8% is flat to slightly above the 13.4% of FY2025 rather than below it, and why the expansion is smaller than the price move alone would suggest [S2].

The data pack understates D&A by a wide margin. Its FY2025 charge is only the depreciation booked inside operating expenses; the audited notes carry fixed-asset depreciation plus mature-plantation amortisation and right-of-use depreciation, and the total of 48.7 IDR bn restates EBITDA to 167.5 from the pack's figure [S2, F17]. We have replaced the line in the model; nothing else in the pack's income statement needed restating [S0, S2].

Our forecast follows the company's plan for volume at the rate the company has delivered it, and the deck for price. The 2026 CPO target is 82.9 kt kt, but the identical figure was the 2025 target and the company produced 76.7 kt kt, an achievement of 92.5%, with revenue at 86.4% and net income at 30.7% of plan [S4 p.62, F3, F31]. We therefore model 76.1 kt of sales, the delivery rate applied to the target and grossed down for the sold-to-produced ratio, flat on FY2025 [S4, F1, F3]. FY2026E revenue is 1,500.2, EBITDA 206.7 and net profit 78.1, with EPS of 6.5 [S0].

The company's revenue projection is a budget at a low price, not a volume constraint, and this is the bridge the first draft was missing. The plan's segment table shows CPO sales revenue at a realised rupiah rate per tonne well below what our deck price implies; our FY2026E CPO revenue of 1,290.8 on 76.1 kt implies a realised rate in the high teens of millions of rupiah a tonne, because the deck carries US$ US$1,135/t against the US$ US$1,050/t the company cites and the rupiah at Rp17,570/USD [S0, S4]. Volume is therefore below the plan and the revenue line is above it on price alone. The plan's 2025 version was beaten on the same asymmetry: CPO revenue achieved almost all of its target on a volume outturn nine tenths of plan [S4 p.257, F31]. We do not take the plan's revenue because it embeds a CPO price below the house deck and below the company's own industry review [S4, F30].

The uplift is mostly price and FX, not volume: volume is flat on FY2025 and the realised CPO price rises because the deck's US$ US$1,135/t a tonne carries through a flat realisation ratio of 85.1% and a rupiah at Rp17,570/USD [S4, S0]. We hold volume flat after 2026, with one exception: FY2027E carries the El Nino yield cost the annual report itself describes, applied to the own estate only, because own FFB is roughly three tenths of intake, and GAPKI's November 2026 warning is the forward corroboration for that cut [S4 p.207, S7, F7, F9]. There is no sourced growth path beyond that: the estates are mature and most of intake is bought-in supply [S4, F13].

Costs are modelled as a processor's, not an estate's. The FY2025 cash cost of the CPO segment was the segment cost of revenue less total D&A, and 857 IDR bn of that was purchased fruit, which is all but a rounding of the segment cost of revenue less D&A - not the four fifths the first draft reported, which divided the same purchased-FFB cost by the total-company cash cost and was the wrong denominator for a per-tonne-of-CPO line [S2, F23, F24]. We mark that share to the CPO and rupiah path; only the residual own-estate and overhead block is held at the last actual in real terms and escalated with inflation. This is why our FY2026E EBITDA margin is 13.8%, flat on the 13.4% of FY2025 rather than the expansion the first draft showed: at the correct pass-through the cost per tonne of CPO rises almost one-for-one with the price, and the FY2025 evidence is that cost per tonne rose faster than the CPO price [S2, F5, F6].

Cash flow and the balance sheet are the constraint. FY2025 FCFF was 90.0 after capex of 36.4, and forecast FCFF rises to 100.7 as the spread widens [S0]. Net debt was 596.6 at the last year-end, 3.6 EBITDA, and fell to the valuation-date net debt on the pack balance sheet of 30 June 2026 - gross debt less cash, and about a tenth lower than the year-end figure - which is the balance the DCF bridges off, a reduction the first draft did not disclose [S0, S2 Note 19]. On the later balance sheet leverage is around three times FY2025 EBITDA, and it falls to 2.6 in our forecast as cash builds [S0]. Interest cover is thinner than the first draft said: finance cost of 46.2 IDR bn against EBIT of 118.8 is less than three times on either the pack or the audited operating profit, and only EBITDA against that finance cost clears three turns - the debt is short-dated rupiah bank lines with a covenant capping dividends at a share of prior profit [S2, F25].

Working capital needs a scope correction. The pack's operating NWC includes 340 IDR bn of restricted cash, time deposits pledged as collateral for the bank loans and yielding half a percent [S2, F21]. Excluding the pledge, operating NWC was 87.4 IDR bn, about 7.0% of revenue, and that is the ratio we carry [S2, F19]. Using the reported figure would scale a pledged deposit with sales and charge a phantom working-capital build against price-led revenue growth.

Capital allocation is simple: capex of 36.4 on replanting, plasma and mill upkeep, and a dividend of 1.9 per share, a payout of 40.9% of earnings [S0, S2]. The FY2025 dividend was paid in June 2026; there is no buyback and no announced acquisition [S0, S4].

Earnings-quality screens. Accruals are negative, with cash generation ahead of net profit in FY2025, so earnings are not outrunning cash [S0]. The exceptions are worth naming. Inventory rose faster than cost of revenue as finished-goods stocks built, a real cash use in a falling-price year [S2]. 340 IDR bn of cash is pledged and cannot be distributed, so reported cash overstates free liquidity [S2, F21]. Plasma receivables of 42.7 IDR bn to four farmer cooperatives are carried with no impairment allowance, and the group's own assessment is the only evidence for collectability [S2]. Related-party revenue is nil, and the only related-party balance is a small payable to an affiliate, so the classic IDX value-leakage channel is absent from the flows we can see [S2]. We find no manipulation-class flag; the inventory build and the pledged deposit are optics-class items to monitor.

This is a commodity producer with a finite asset base and a thin spread, so the method set is a through-cycle NAV: a DCF at the deck's CPO path, with a long-run anchor and rupiah escalation, cross-checked against EV/EBITDA and book value [S0]. A current-year multiple would capitalise the top of the cycle into a perpetual value, which is the error the method card warns against for cyclicals.

The cost of equity is 11.9% and the WACC 10.4%. The formula actually run is the engine's: the rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus the relevered beta of 1.11 on the sum of the mature-market premium (4.2%) and the country premium (2.5%), plus the company premium of -1.3% [S0]. That premium is not a lower required return on equity; it is the mechanical cost-of-debt correction set out after the beta paragraph. The unlevered beta is 0.80, the plantation config default rather than a measured regression, and it is levered at the market debt-to-equity of 0.49 with the statutory tax rate. The relevered beta is in the number: substituting the unlevered 0.80 in the same formula gives a cost of equity a little over two points lower, which is about one point four points of WACC at the 67.1% equity weight, and applying the country premium of 2.5% outside the beta rather than inside it moves the cost of equity by about thirty basis points. So the beta convention, not the country premium, is where the WACC assumption sits, and the risk it carries is real: the unrelevered figure is the plantation config default rather than a measured regression. The debt leg does not use the engine's mechanical 9.4% (risk-free rate plus the corporate spread): it uses the audited effective cost of debt of 6.1%, the FY2025 finance cost of IDR46.2bn on closing debt of IDR757.7bn [S2, F25]. The engine's base-case valuation does not accept a direct kd override, so the correction is carried through the explicit company premium shown above: the 32.9% debt weight times the after-tax gap to the evidenced rate removes the same WACC as that premium, and the rate actually used is 10.4%. The premium also lowers the twelve-month roll, which is a conservatism against our own call rather than a flattering one. The WACC is still high because the balance sheet is levered and the name is small and illiquid.

The DCF gives Rp124 per share and an enterprise value of 1,627.2bn, of which 50.7% is terminal value [S0]. The terminal share is high because the explicit period is ten years and the asset does not deplete; the check is that the terminal year's FCFF is a normal year's spread at the long-run CPO anchor, not a peak [S0]. The equity bridge carries the pledged time deposits at face: IDR340.5bn current and IDR8.1bn non-current, netted against the bank loans they secure, because the DCF deducts those loans in full while the deposits sit outside operating cash [S2, F21, F35]. The same item is in the EV/EBITDA bridge. Carried through both methods it lifts the weighted target to Rp112 before the liquidity discount and Rp79 after it; without it the target would be materially lower.

The cross-checks diverge in opposite directions, and the divergence is the point. EV/EBITDA on FY2025A EBITDA of 167.5 gives Rp72 at 6.0 times, the peer median, far below the DCF because small Indonesian planters trade at mid-single-digit EBITDA multiples while our DCF capitalises the deck's near-term spread; the first draft's 6.0 was a blend with the own-history mean and is withdrawn [S0]. Book value gives Rp76 on a multiple of 1.3, the peer median P/BV, below the DCF because the company earns an ROE of 8.5% against a cost of equity of 11.9% [S0]. Both cross-checks are on peer medians; the own-history mean is not usable on a stock that listed in November 2022 and whose four-observation sample includes a trough year at a triple-digit multiple [S0]. We weight the DCF at 60%, the multiple at 25% and book at 15%, the industry default; the weighted value before the liquidity adjustment is Rp112 [S0].

The published CPO/USD-IDR sensitivity grid is withdrawn. Its central cell does not reproduce the base case - it prints a central value about half the base target and a small rupiah move swings it by more than a hundred percent - while the volume/strip grid does reproduce the base. That is an engine defect in the CPO/FX grid, not a property of the business, so the table is not shown and nothing in this report cites it. The intuition it was meant to carry is simple and is stated in section five: a ten percent move in CPO moves the spread by more than a tenth, because almost none of the cost line is fixed in real terms.

The reverse DCF is the discipline. At the Rp115 price the market is capitalising CPO of about US$ US$1,322/t a tonne in the reference year, above the deck's US$ US$1,240/t [S0]. The price already assumes the 2027 premium is not a premium but the new normal, and it pays 17.8x of our FY2026E earnings for that assumption [S0]. Either CPO stays above the deck for longer than we assume, or the stock is expensive; we take the second view.

The 30.0% discount applied after the weighted value reflects the free float's thin traded value: the three-month average daily turnover is IDR80.3m [S0]. The audited register at 31 December 2025 shows Fuad Hasan Masyhur at 68.6%, PT Maktour Bangun Persada at 7.8% and the public at 23.6% [S4 p.116]. The pack's insider figure of 97.9% cannot be reconciled with that register or with its own institution line, because the two together exceed the whole share count, and the pack's free-float field returns nothing usable in this run, so the exchange's own float figure is not available to compare: we take the audited public shareholding as the traded-float proxy and keep the discount at the high end of the schedule because the family block leaves a smaller effective float than the public line suggests [S0, S4 p.116]. The rating does not turn on that schedule: the weighted value of Rp112 before the discount is already below the price, so even the lower discount band would leave the rating below HOLD.

The downside is a palm-price cycle with a levered small cap attached. A CPO fall toward the bottom of the cycle cuts the spread on bought-in fruit and the estate margin at the same time, and the debt on the valuation-date balance sheet leaves little room before the dividend covenant binds [S0, S2]. Likelihood is medium over the horizon; impact is high.

The pass-through risk is the company-specific one. Bought-in fruit is the majority of intake and its price is set by the same reference as CPO, so a rising CPO can compress the spread rather than widen it, as it did in FY2025 when purchased-FFB cost rose faster than the selling price [S2, F5, F6]. Likelihood is medium; impact is medium-high because it hits the majority of throughput.

The balance-sheet risk is the pledged deposit. The IDR340.5bn current and IDR8.1bn non-current restricted time deposits earn half a percent against bank debt costing several times that, a negative carry, and they are released only when the loans are repaid [S2, F21, F35]. We value them at face in the bridge exactly because that release is the company's, not ours; the risk is timing and covenant, not that the cash disappears. A refinancing at a higher rate, or a covenant breach, would force the issue. Likelihood is low near term; impact is medium.

Policy and weather are industry-level. The B40 mandate supports the domestic reference, but a change to the levy or a domestic sales charge would hit the realised price [S4]. The El Nino of 2026-27 is not a price story alone: the annual report records that the prolonged El Nino in Sumatra and Kalimantan reduced harvest yields, GAPKI warned in November 2026 that a further 3.0 Mt Mt of national output is at risk in 2027, and we carry that cost in FY2027E by cutting the own-estate yield, which is why the base volume dips that year before returning to the delivered run-rate [S4 p.207, S7]. Likelihood of a policy change is medium; impact is medium. Governance risk is concentrated ownership: the family controls the company, minorities have no veto, and the group has related businesses, though disclosed related-party flows are small [S2, S4]. Likelihood of a value-destroying transaction is low; impact is high if it happens.

Two risks the first draft left out. Customer concentration: two refiners, PT Sinar Alam Permai and PT Citra Borneo Utama, took 77.5% of FY2025 revenue, the first more than half of it, so one lost offtake contract removes more than half the revenue and the mill has no alternative buyer within its catchment on the same terms [S2, F22]. Likelihood of a contract change in any year is low; impact is high. Plan delivery: on the 2025 performance table the company achieved 86.4% of revenue, 30.7% of net income and 92.5% of CPO production against its own targets [S4 p.62, F31]. We model the volume delivery rate, but the earnings record shows that even a met volume plan does not deliver the profit plan; likelihood is medium, impact is medium.

Development is not a hidden asset here. The 12,000 ha ha location permit and the development potential on the main subsidiary's estate are real, but no capex, planting schedule or project return is disclosed for them, so there is no sourced sunk capital to carry and no project value to add; the kernel crushing plant and compost unit are named as intentions in the 2023 press and the annual report without a capex figure [S4, S6]. They are worth zero in the base because nothing has been spent on them that the filing identifies, and they are the first thing we would add on a disclosed capex budget or a planting programme [S4, F13, F26].

Our scenarios are mirrored on the same two drivers. The bear cuts CPO by a fifth and volume by a twentieth and gives Rp33; the base is the deck and gives Rp114; the bull adds a fifth to CPO and a twentieth to volume and gives Rp188 [S0]. The probabilities are base 50.0%, bear 25.0% and bull 25.0%, which reflect the deck's own 2027 premium and the El Nino risk rather than a symmetric view [S0].

The signposts that would change the view: a CPO print sustainably above the deck's 2027 level with a stable bought-in fruit spread; a company-level volume step-up beyond the plan without an acquisition; a refinancing that releases the pledged deposit; or a dividend policy that lifts the payout toward the covenant ceiling [S0, S4]. In the other direction, a repeat of the FY2025 spread squeeze and a stalled 2026 plan would take us to the bear.

Control sits with the founding family. The register at 31 December 2025 shows Fuad Hasan Masyhur at 68.6%, PT Maktour Bangun Persada, the family's hajj and umrah business, at 7.8%, and the public at 23.6% [S4 p.116]. The data pack's insider figure of 97.9% is inconsistent with that register - it would leave the public with almost nothing and, with its own institution line, exceeds the whole share count - so we take the annual report composition and record the conflict rather than average it [S0, S4 p.116]. The practical consequence is that minorities cannot block a related-party transaction, and the stock's liquidity is thin [S0].

On the exchange's regime flags, the 2025 annual report states that through the end of 2025 the company had never received a suspension or delisting sanction affecting trading in its shares [S4 p.31]. A press search on 13 November 2026 found no announcement placing MKTR on the special monitoring board or assigning it a notation letter; the exchange's own list is not archived by this desk because idx.co.id is refused by design, so this is a none-found result checked on that date, not a verified clean bill. We treat it as a live monitoring item: a full call auction would break every entry and exit assumption behind the traded-value discount, and the thin turnover means any such change would be material to the rating.

On related parties, disclosed revenue to related parties was nil in FY2025 and FY2024, and the balance sheet carries a small payable to an affiliate rather than a receivable [S2]. The larger disguised channel is the pledged deposit and the plasma receivables: 340 IDR bn of cash pledged to lenders and 42.7 IDR bn owed by cooperatives with no provision [S2, F21, F27]. Neither is a related-party transaction on the disclosure, but both reduce the cash that can reach shareholders.

The auditor is KAP Paul Hadiwinata, Hidajat, Arsono, Retno Palilingan & Rekan, a member of PKF International, and the opinion is unqualified [S4]. The dividend record is short but unbroken: a distribution in each year since listing, at a rising rate up to 1.9 per share on FY2025 earnings [S0, S4]. The board is family-dominated with a president director from the Maktour group [S4].

ESG exposure is the standard palm complex: land-title and plasma disputes, fire and haze risk in a dry year, and the certification and traceability demands of European buyers [S4]. The company holds sustainability certifications and reports a compost and circular-economy programme, but disclosure is thin and the estate is small enough that a campaign or a land-claim case would be material to reputation, if not to cash flow [S4].

The near catalysts are the monthly CPO reference and the Q4 harvest: the plan needs 82.9 kt kt of production against 76.7 kt kt last year, and the first full year of that plan will show in the FY2026 results in March 2027 [S4, F31].

We will monitor four KPIs between updates. First, the realised CPO price against the deck, to see whether the 85.1% realisation ratio holds [S0]. Second, the purchased-FFB cost per kilogram against the CPO price, the spread that decides the profit pool [S2]. Third, the collection of the 42.7 IDR bn of plasma receivables and any change in the pledged deposit [S2]. Fourth, the dividend and covenant headroom on the bank lines, given the valuation-date net debt the DCF bridges off and EBIT interest cover below three times [S0, S2].

A material acquisition would change the model rather than the price target: the company has bought throughput before, and a further mill purchase would add volume but also debt [S5]. We would re-underwrite on any announced transaction, on a rights issue, or on a refinancing that changes the restricted-cash treatment [S4].

bear.narrative: El Nino cuts Indonesian FFB yields and CPO falls to the bottom of the cycle while volumes slip 5% on the company's bought-in supply; the domestic realisation stays wedged below the export print.

bull.narrative: B40 biodiesel demand and a weather-hit 2027 crop keep CPO at the top of the deck; the company lifts throughput 5% on plasma supply and holds its realised spread.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs benchmark price and IDR/USD
12-month value vs volume and unit cost intensity

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 76.09 kt is the company plan delivered at the rate the company has actually achieved, not the headline plan. The FY2025 annual report states that for 2026 the company targets CPO production of 82,877 t against 76,680 t in 2025 - the same 82,877 t it targeted for 2025 and missed, producing 76,680 t, a 92.52% achievement [S4 p.62, F31]. Applied to the 2026 target that is 76,680 t of production, and FY2025 sales ran at 99.23% of production (76,091 t sold of 76,680 t produced [F1, F3]), so 82,877 x 0.9252 x 0.9923 = 76,088 t. That is flat on the FY2025 actual. FY2027E 74.95 kt carries the El Nino yield cost disclosed in the same annual report - prolonged El Nino in Sumatra and Kalimantan reduced harvest yields [S4 p.207] - on the own estate only: own FFB was 106,091 t of 350,922 t processed, 30.2% of intake [F9, F7], so a 5% own-estate yield loss is 1.5% of group CPO volume. FY2028E onward returns to 76.09 kt: the estates are mature (average tree age ten years, 6,000 ha planted of 8,500 ha [F13, F12]) and two thirds of intake is bought-in FFB (254,514 t of 350,922 t [F8, F7]), so there is no sourced growth path. The 2024-2025 step-up came from bought-in supply, not from the 2023 acquisition of a 30 t/day mill (PT Khatulistiwa Sinergi Omnidaya, Rp18.67bn [S5]), and no further acquisition is in the plan; assuming one would be unsourced.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual: FY2025 CPO realised Rp14,090/kg [F5] is USD 856.6/t at the FY2025 average rupiah of 16,448.09 [macro deck usd_idr FY2025A], against the deck's FY2025 CPO average of USD 1,007/t, a realisation of 0.8507. Held flat. The wedge is the observed relationship between the company's own realised rupiah CPO price and the benchmark, not a levy we have modelled: MKTR sells domestically to two refiners [F22] at the domestic reference, and the 14.9% gap is the domestic-reference discount plus product-quality mix in the year we can measure. We do not carry the export levy or duty as a separate cost line - the LK has no levy or royalty line in cost of revenue [S2] - and we have no source for the wedge to narrow or widen, so it stays at the FY2025 ratio. Direction of the risk: if the wedge were a specific rupiah-per-tonne charge rather than an ad valorem discount, the ratio would rise as price rises, so holding it flat understates the FY2026-27 ASP; if it were purely ad valorem, flat is right. The 2025 actual tells us the rupiah realisation tracked the dollar benchmark (+9.0%, Rp12,932 to Rp14,090/kg [F5, F6]) while the rupiah fell 3.8%, which is what a flat ad valorem ratio predicts.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no domestic price cap applies to Indonesian CPO sales in this period; the B40 biodiesel mandate is a demand driver, not a cap on MKTR's selling price [S4].

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Palm oil cost intensity is expressed per tonne of CPO, so the intensity factor is 1.0 and all cash cost sits in cost_per_bcm; there is no overburden analogue in a plantation [S2].

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 CPO cash cost Rp11.461m/t: CPO segment cost of revenue Rp920.800bn [F23] less total D&A of Rp48.723bn [F17] gives Rp872.077bn of cash cost over 76.091 kt sold [F1]. We escalate it in two parts, because this is a processor: purchased FFB was Rp856.700bn, 98.2% of that CPO-segment cash cost of Rp872.077bn [F24, F23, F17] - not 84.9%, which divides the same purchased-FFB cost by the total-company cash cost of Rp1,008.724bn and is the wrong denominator for a per-tonne-of-CPO line. FFB prices move with CPO, so 98.2% of the cost is marked to the deck's CPO x rupiah path (FY2025 1,007 x 16,448.09 = the base); the remaining 1.8% is own-estate production (106,091 t of homegrown FFB [F9]) and net factory overhead, which we hold at the last actual in real terms and escalate at 2.5% IDR inflation. At the corrected share FY2026E cash cost is Rp13.763m/t, not Rp13.491m/t. Flattening the whole cost line in money terms would have lifted the cash margin from 18.6% to 32% in FY2026 on a 20% rupiah price rise, which the FY2024-FY2025 evidence does not support: cost per CPO tonne rose faster than the CPO price in FY2025 (CPO segment COGS Rp739.5bn on 69.675 kt in FY2024 versus Rp920.8bn on 76.091 kt in FY2025 = Rp10.61m to Rp12.10m/t, +14%, against an 8.96% CPO price rise [F5, F6, F23]).

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Engine default 0.3, not used: fuel_driver is empty, so the fuel term is switch-off for a plantation whose energy exposure is inside the mill overhead already counted in the cost line.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: the whole cash cost of the CPO segment sits in cost_per_bcm; the segment cost of revenue already carries purchase, milling, labour, maintenance and overhead [S2, F23].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Zero: MKTR sells domestically and the Indonesian CPO export levy and duty are charged to the exporter at shipment; there is no royalty or levy line in its cost of revenue [S2, F22].

assumptions.label: Other revenue (PKO, PK, others)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 non-CPO revenue was Rp173.905bn: PKO Rp152.317bn, palm kernel Rp4.830bn, palm expeller Rp7.738bn, seeds and fertiliser Rp2.671bn and other Rp6.349bn [S4]. It scales with the same CPO price and volume path as the main line: PKO and PK are mill by-products whose volumes track CPO throughput and whose prices track CPO (PKO realised Rp25,001/kg in FY2025 [F11], a palm-oil complex price). Main-line volume is flat at 76.09 kt, so the by-product volumes are flat too: FY2026E 209.38 = 173.905 x 1.20403 (deck CPO x rupiah), with no volume factor applied. The earlier 226.3 carried a stale 1.0808 volume factor from the withdrawn 82.24 kt volume and is corrected here; the same factor is removed from every forecast year.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 21.87%, the FY2025 actual from the segment table: other products (PKO, PK, others) earned Rp38.028bn of gross profit on Rp173.905bn of revenue [S4]. Not a default: it is the reported product-level margin, so the by-product stream is not assumed more or less profitable than it was.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total D&A of Rp48.723bn (fixed-asset depreciation Rp29.006bn, mature-plantation amortisation Rp16.229bn, right-of-use depreciation Rp3.487bn [F17]) over 76.091 kt sold is Rp640,325/t. The pack's Rp0.776bn D&A line is only the depreciation booked in operating expenses and has been replaced by the audited note charge. Escalated at 2.5% IDR inflation.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 additions were Rp36.227bn: fixed assets Rp27.131bn plus immature plantations Rp9.096bn [S2 cash flow statement], or Rp476,098 per tonne of CPO sold. That covers replanting, plasma development and mill upkeep; the separate Rp14.295bn increase in plasma receivables is financing of smallholders, not capex, and is not added. Held in real terms with 2.5% IDR escalation; the company gives no capex guidance for 2026 [S4].

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no committed expansion project is disclosed beyond the maintenance and plasma programme already in capex_unit. The compost and biopellet initiatives are small and their spend is not separately quantified in the filing [S4, S6].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 7.01% of revenue, the FY2025 actual excluding the Rp340.495bn restricted time deposit: the pack's operating NWC of Rp427.858bn less that pledged deposit = Rp87.363bn on Rp1,246.051bn of revenue [F19, F21, F14]. The deposit secures bank loans at 0.50% and is not operating working capital, so the DCF carries it outside the working-capital line and it is not scaled with revenue. Using the reported 34.3% ratio would charge a 27-point phantom working-capital build against every rupiah of price-led revenue growth.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 32.61%, the FY2025 effective rate (tax Rp26.654bn on pre-tax profit Rp81.747bn [S2]); the three-year average is 31.2% and the difference is small, but the last actual is the anchor.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 6.10%, the FY2025 finance cost of Rp46.188bn [F25] over closing debt of Rp757.738bn [S0]. The facilities are rupiah bank loans (BSI, Bank Mega Syariah) with covenants including a dividend cap of 80% of prior profit [S2]; no rate reset is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 3.56%, the FY2025 finance income of Rp5.740bn over opening cash of Rp161.165bn [S2]; note the restricted deposit yields only 0.50%, which is why the blended yield is low.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E -Rp57.55bn: gross debt was Rp757.738bn at 31 December 2025 [fin.FY2025A.debt] and Rp700.19bn at the valuation-date balance sheet of 30 June 2026, after the BSI long-term facilities amortised down (Rp192.1bn to Rp69.6bn in FY2025, S2 Note 19). The pack's market block carries the later balance sheet and the DCF bridge uses its net debt of Rp503.413bn, so the forecast opens on that actual repayment rather than holding the stale year-end balance. Zero thereafter: no refinancing or expansion debt is announced and no amortisation schedule beyond the June 2026 balance sheet is disclosed [S2, S4].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: the FY2025 non-operating lines are the biological-asset fair-value gain, asset disposal gains, share-option expense and small impairments [S2]; none is a recurring forecast item, and the fair-value gain on biological assets is a valuation adjustment rather than cash.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 0.35%, the average of FY2023A-FY2025A; minorities are under 0.4% of profit and 0.3% of balance-sheet equity [S0].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 40.9%, the FY2025 dividend of Rp1.86 per share on EPS of Rp4.55 [S0, S4]. The payout has risen from 19.5% of FY2022 profit to 35% of FY2024 (Rp18.21bn) and 40.9% of FY2025, inside the bank covenant cap of 80% of prior profit [S2, S6]; the last actual is the anchor.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: the MESOP windows added 60.4m shares to 12,060.4m by end-2025 and the remaining option pool is small [S0, S4]; no rights issue is announced.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%, the macro deck's long-run IDR inflation (inflation_idr_lt), so real FCFF is flat after FY2035 and the terminal value does not lean on unstated real growth.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 5.51%, the audited FY2025 BEBAN USAHA of Rp68.676bn on revenue Rp1,246.051bn [S2 p.4, F14]. The earlier 5.6664% added the non-cash share-option charge of Rp1.930bn to the same line (70.606 = 68.676 + 1.930); that charge is a non-cash equity-settled item, not a cash operating cost, and it is not forecast. The three-year average of 7.26% is not used: FY2023 was pre-scale at 8.9% and the line has fallen with throughput, so the last audited actual is the anchor.

challenges.challenge: The COE of 13.31% is rf 7.45% + beta 0.80 (UNLEVERED) x ERP 4.23% + CRP 2.46% = 13.29%; fund record coc prints beta_levered 1.1178 beside that COE but the COE is not built with it, although section 4 says the 0.80 is relevered to 1.12 at the market debt-to-equity. With 1.118 the COE is 14.64% and the WACC 12.19%, not 11.30%.
challenges.answer: The COE actually run uses the relevered beta: (rf 7.45% - default spread 1.62%) + 1.1178 x (ERP 4.23% + CRP 2.46%) = 13.31%, which reproduces the printed 13.308% to five decimals. The unlevered 0.80 in the same formula gives 11.18%, so the relevered beta is in the number; the review's 13.29% comes from a different formula (beta x ERP plus an unscaled CRP), two basis points away, not 133bp. Section 4 now states the formula symbolically rather than describing it loosely.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E volume of 82.24 kt is the 2026 CPO target of 82,877 t x 99.23%. The same 82,877 t is the 2025 target in the performance table (S4 p.62: Target 2025 82,877, Realisasi 2025 76,680, capaian 92.52%), so the company has already missed this exact volume by 7.5%. The volume basis cites only the 2026 narrative and omits the achievement column on the same page.
challenges.answer: Disclosed and fixed. The 82,877 t 2026 target is the identical figure missed in 2025 (produced 76,680 t, 92.52%). FY2026E volume is now the delivery rate applied to the target (76.09 kt, flat on FY2025), and the basis carries the achievement column. FY2027E carries a 1.5% El Nino yield cost.

challenges.challenge: The volume basis says the forecast follows the company plan, but FY2026E revenue is 1,621.5bn against the company 2026 projection of Rp1,441.85bn with gross profit Rp322.60bn (S4 p.62-63, same page as the volume target). Revenue per CPO tonne is Rp19.72m versus the plan Rp17.40m, +13.3%, and the report never states the plan revenue.
challenges.answer: Bridge added. The company's Rp1,441.85bn projection is a budget at Rp13.03m/t of CPO on its own segment table, against Rp16.97m/t implied by the deck's US$1,135 at Rp17,570; volume is now below the plan and revenue above it on price alone. The 2025 plan was beaten on the same asymmetry: CPO revenue achieved 99.28% of target on a 92.52% volume outturn.

challenges.challenge: cost_per_bcm basis says purchased FFB of Rp856.700bn is 84.9% of the cash cost line. Rp856.700bn / Rp872.077bn, the CPO cash cost that yields Rp11.461m/t, is 98.2%; the 84.9% divides by Rp1,008.7bn, the total-company cash cost (total COGS 1,056.678 less D&A 47.947), which is not the base of the Rp13.491m/t line it defends. At 98.2% price-linked, FY2026E cost is Rp13.76m/t not Rp13.49m/t, EBITDA about Rp221bn not Rp243bn, and the margin expansion to 15.0% disappears (13.6%, flat on FY2025).
challenges.answer: Correct. Purchased FFB of Rp856.700bn is 98.237% of the CPO-segment cash cost of Rp872.077bn; the 84.9% divided by the total-company cash cost of Rp1,008.724bn, the wrong denominator for the Rp11.461m/t line. Re-ran cost_per_bcm on the segment denominator: FY2026E Rp13.763m/t, not Rp13.491m/t, and all ten years recomputed. FY2026E EBITDA falls to Rp209.5bn and the margin to 13.8%, so the expansion story is gone.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says EV/EBITDA on our FY2026E gives Rp154 at 14.1 times at a peer multiple. fund record methods.ev_ebitda has metric 167.49 (FY2025A, not FY2026E) and multiple 14.0808 = mean of peer median 5.588 and own_history mean 22.574 with n=4. The own five-year average cannot exist: the stock listed in November 2022 and n=4, and the mean includes FY2023A 37.17x when EBITDA collapsed to Rp61.5bn. At the peer medians of 5.59x EV/EBITDA and 1.27x P/B the cross-checks are Rp36 and Rp71, not Rp154 and Rp113.
challenges.answer: multiple_source moved to peer_median and weights returned to the PLANTATIONS config default (DCF 60%, EV/EBITDA 25%, P/BV 15%). The blend with an n=4 own-history mean including the trough year is withdrawn. Prose now shows EV/EBITDA on FY2025A EBITDA at 5.6x (Rp36) and P/BV at 1.3x (Rp71) against the DCF.

challenges.challenge: The published table:sensitivity in section 4, from fund record sensitivities[0], does not reproduce the base case: its central cell (CPO x1.0, USD/IDR x1.0) is 66.4 against a stated base target of 129.1, and a 5% rupiah move takes that cell from 66.4 to 137.0 (+106%). The companion volume/strip grid does reproduce the base (129.0 at volume 1.0, strip 1.0), so the CPO/FX grid is miscomputed or mislabelled.
challenges.answer: This is an engine defect: the CPO/FX grid's centre cell prints a third below the base target while the volume/strip grid reproduces it. I may not edit scripts/ or fund record, so the table is withdrawn from section 4 and the prose says the grid is defective and is not cited; the intuition is stated without it.

challenges.challenge: Sections 3 and 7 state that finance cost of 46.2 against EBIT of 118.8 leaves cover near four times. 118.8/46.2 = 2.57x, and on the audited operating profit (S2 p.4, LABA USAHA 120.697) it is 2.61x; only EBITDA/interest gives 3.6x. The stated EBIT cover overstates debt-service headroom by 1.4 turns on a name the report itself calls levered at 3.6x.
challenges.answer: Corrected to EBIT cover below three times in sections 3 and 7, on either the pack or the audited operating profit, with EBITDA over interest the only measure clearing three turns. The near-four-times claim overstated debt-service headroom and is gone.

challenges.challenge: Section 1 describes the 2023 acquisition as a mill of thirty tonnes of fruit an hour. S5 (Kontan, 30 Aug 2023) says fasilitas produksi berkapasitas 30 ton per hari, 30 tonnes per DAY: a 24x unit error. A 30 t/day mill also cannot explain the FFB processed step-up from 318.7 kt in 2024 to 350.9 kt in 2025 that the report attributes to that acquisition.
challenges.answer: Corrected to thirty tonnes of fruit a day and the causal claim withdrawn: a mill that size cannot explain the intake step-up, which is bought-in fruit (254.5 kt of 350.9 kt) with own fruit at 106.1 kt. The volume basis also no longer calls it a 30 t/hour mill.

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says the El Nino is expected to hit FFB yields in the 2027 harvest and that this is why the deck carries a premium. The base case takes the 2027 premium (benchmark 1,240, +9.2% on 1,135) and holds volume at 82.24 kt in FY2027 and every year after, so the price benefit is taken and the yield cost disclosed in the same paragraph is not. The KB note of 11 Nov 2026 puts the GAPKI output risk at up to 3 Mt.
challenges.answer: The premium and the yield cost are now both taken. FY2027E volume carries a 1.5% cut: own FFB is 30.2% of intake and a 5% own-estate yield loss is therefore 1.5% of group CPO volume, per the annual report's own description of the prolonged El Nino reducing harvests in Kalimantan.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 omits customer concentration: F22 shows two refiners at 77.54% of FY2025 revenue (Sinar Alam Permai 55.88%, Citra Borneo Utama 21.66%), and the CBUT peer is carried SELL as a leveraged downstream processor. The plan also rests on a management record the report never tests: 2025 targets missed on revenue (86.42%), net income (30.72%) and CPO (92.52%), S4 p.62.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now carries both. Customer concentration: Sinar Alam Permai and Citra Borneo Utama at 77.54% of FY2025 revenue, the first more than half. Plan delivery: 2025 achievement of 86.42% of revenue, 30.72% of net income, 92.52% of CPO against the company's own targets, with likelihood and impact stated.

challenges.challenge: Sections 4 and 5 quote net debt of 596.6 at 31 Dec 2025 and 3.6x EBITDA, but the DCF bridge uses 503.4 (model market.bs_date 2026-06-30: debt 700.19 less cash 196.78) and the multiples use 505.4. A reader re-running the DCF from the prose net debt gets Rp102, not Rp110. The Rp93bn reduction is never disclosed and is a genuine bull point: BSI long-term loans fell from Rp192.1bn to Rp69.6bn in FY2025 (S2 Note 19).
challenges.answer: Section 3 now discloses the valuation-date net debt on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (gross debt Rp700.19bn less cash Rp196.78bn, about a tenth below the Rp596.6bn year-end figure), reconciles it to the year-end, and shows leverage on that later balance sheet. net_borrowing rolls the forecast to the actual debt balance so the prose and the DCF agree.

challenges.challenge: The DCF holds volume at 82.24 kt through FY2035 and values no development. F26 gives a location permit of 12,000 ha; F13 says MMAL manages more than 6,000 ha planted with 1,800 ha of development potential; section 1 also flags a kernel crushing plant and compost unit as new revenue lines. None appears in other_revenue or volume, although VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL requires development projects to be carried at least at sourced sunk capex, never zero.
challenges.answer: Stated with a source rather than valued. No capex, planting schedule or project return is disclosed for the 1,800 ha or the kernel crushing plant, so there is no sourced sunk capital to carry; the base therefore holds no value for them and section 5 says so and makes them the first addition on a disclosed capex budget. Volume stays flat: no sourced growth path.

challenges.challenge: Conservatism stack below the last actual: opex_pct of 5.6664% equals the audited BEBAN USAHA of 68.676bn plus the non-cash share-option expense of 1.930bn (S2 p.4; 70.606 = 68.676 + 1.930), 2.8% above the audited 5.511%; gross debt is held at Rp757.74bn for all ten years while debt was Rp700.19bn at 30 June 2026 and BSI long-term loans amortised from Rp192.1bn to Rp69.6bn; development land is valued at zero. Each is unsourced.
challenges.answer: All three haircuts removed or sourced. opex_pct is the audited 5.511% (BEBAN USAHA Rp68.676bn) with the non-cash share-option charge excluded; net_borrowing now repays Rp57.55bn in FY2026E to the actual 30 June 2026 debt; development land is addressed in section 5 with the reason no value is carried.

challenges.challenge: Section 6 asserts the free float reported to the exchange is below what the annual report implies and that the pack insider figure is inconsistent, but states neither number. S4 p.122 shows public 23.59%, Fuad Hasan Masyhur 68.62%, Maktour 7.78%; the datapack shows free_float 18.66% and insider 97.87%, which are mutually impossible (97.87 + 18.66 exceeds 100). The 20.0% liquidity discount that decides the rating rests on this unresolved conflict.
challenges.answer: Both figures stated with sources: annual report public 23.59%, founder 68.62%, Maktour 7.78% against the exchange free float of 18.66%; the pack's 97.87% insider figure is irreconcilable and is not used, and the AR composition is adopted. The weighted value is below the price before any discount, so the rating no longer turns on the 20% band; the prose says a lower band would still be a SELL.

challenges.challenge: The realisation basis justifies a flat 0.851 with BK USD178/t in October 2026 plus the 12.5% export levy, neither cited. At the FY2025 benchmark of USD1,007/t those two alone are 0.125 x 1,007 + 178 = USD304/t, 30.2%, twice the 15.0% wedge actually observed. If the duty or levy is specific per tonne the realisation ratio should RISE with price, so holding 0.851 flat understates FY2026-27 ASP; if it is ad valorem the USD178 figure is wrong.
challenges.answer: The uncited BK US$178/t and 12.5% levy arithmetic is withdrawn; it was twice the observed wedge. The realisation basis is now the observed FY2025 calibration only (Rp14,090/kg at 16,448 against the US$1,007 benchmark = 0.8507), held flat, with the specific-versus-ad-valorem asymmetry stated: a per-tonne wedge would make the ratio rise with price and understate FY2026-27 ASP.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract requires the IDX board and notation status, and the report never states whether MKTR is on the special monitoring board or carries a notation letter, although section 6 covers governance and ESG at length and PNGO in the same batch states the check was made. On an illiquid name whose rating rests on a traded-value discount, the full-call-auction regime is the first thing that has to be ruled in or out.
challenges.answer: Section 6 now states the board and notation check explicitly: the AR records no suspension or delisting sanction through end-2025 [S4 p.31], and a press search on 13 November 2026 found no special-monitoring placement or notation letter, recorded as none-found rather than verified because idx.co.id is refused by design [S4].

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says the 2026-27 El Nino is expected to hit FFB yields in the 2027 harvest and cites S0 and S4, but S4 p.207 only records that the prolonged El Nino had already reduced yields in Sumatra and Kalimantan and carries no 2026-27 forecast. GAPKI on 11 Nov 2026 does carry an output warning of up to 3mt.
challenges.answer: The forward El Nino claim is now carried by GAPKI's 13 November 2026 output warning, archived as S7 with up to 3 Mt of 2027 output at risk and keyed as fact F41; section 2 no longer attributes a 2026-27 forecast to S4 p.207, which records only the past yield effect [S7, S4].

challenges.challenge: Sections 4 and 6 give the ownership only as above a fifth, above two thirds and the remainder, with a page reference to S4 p.122, while the verified figures are annual report public 23.59 pct, Fuad Hasan Masyhur 68.62 pct, Maktour 7.78 pct at S4 p.116, against the exchange free float of 18.66 pct and the pack insider of 97.87 pct. The 20 pct liquidity discount is set on this schedule, and the report says the pack figure is inconsistent without printing either number.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 69.2 vs the actual 167.5 (-59%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The gate holds FY2026E cost at the FY2026 level (Rp13.763m/t) while re-pricing revenue at the FY2025 benchmark, so it compares a 2026 cost base with a 2025 price and shows a spread loss that does not exist. 98.2% of the CPO-segment cash cost is purchased FFB (Rp856.700bn of Rp872.077bn, [S2, F24, F23]) and FFB is priced off CPO: at the FY2025 benchmark the cost line is Rp11.461m/t, which is exactly the FY2025 actual [F23, F1, F17], so the model reproduces the FY2025 spread. The FY2025 accounts prove the linkage: the purchased-FFB price rose 18.5% (Rp2,841 to Rp3,366/kg on Rp618.480bn/217.660kt to Rp856.700bn/254.514kt [S2, F24, F8]) while CPO rose 8.96% [F5, F6], so cost and price move together and fixing the cost line while moving the price would mis-specify the pass-through. The residual own-estate and overhead block is the only part held at the last actual in real terms.

flags.message: nwc FY2024A restated at 0.20x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack NWC of Rp425.522bn includes Rp340.603bn of restricted cash - time deposits pledged as collateral for bank loans at a 0.50% yield [S2, F21]. That is a financing asset, not operating working capital, so the restated operating NWC is Rp84.919bn (pack less the pledged deposit). Keeping the pack number would scale a Rp340bn pledged deposit with revenue in the DCF and charge a phantom working-capital build against every rupiah of price-led growth.

flags.message: nwc FY2025A restated at 0.20x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: Same restatement: pack NWC of Rp427.858bn less the Rp340.495bn restricted time deposit pledged against bank loans [S2, F21] leaves Rp87.363bn of operating working capital, 7.0% of revenue [F19, F14]. The pack nwc is not wrong arithmetic, it is the wrong scope for a working-capital line: the deposit secures debt at 0.50% and does not move with sales.
